Provision: RESTRICTIVE GOVERNANCE PROVISION 1. [Government] [must] [create or appoint agency to implement and enforce the law] [at law’s commencement] [or else it is negligent in its duties]
Evidence: Article 19(2): "The body that has rendered a decision on state registration of a charitable organization shall exert control over the compliance of activity of the charitable organization with the goals for the sake of which it has been established."
Explanation: The statute itself designates the same authority that performs state registration as the body responsible for ongoing control and enforcement of the law. By assigning this mandate in the text that comes into force with the law, the legislature has effectively *appointed* an implementing-and-enforcing agency at the moment of the law’s commencement. This satisfies the ADICO elements: (A) Government/legislature, (D) shall, (I) appoint an enforcement body, (C) built into the law’s entry into force. Therefore the provision is correctly coded as present (1).

Provision: RESTRICTIVE GOVERNANCE PROVISION 2. [CSOs] [must] [accept restricted freedoms on certain matters] [after law’s commencement] [or else face penalty for non-compliance]
Evidence: Article 12(3): "A charitable organization shall have the right to engage in business activities only to achieve the goals, for the sake of which it was set up…"; Article 12(5): "A charitable organization shall not have the right to spend its means and to use its property for rendering support to the political parties, movements, groups and campaigns."
Explanation: The statute imposes explicit substantive limits on what charitable organizations may do: they may conduct business activities only for their statutory goals and are prohibited from financially supporting political parties or campaigns. These clauses clearly require CSOs to accept restrictions on their freedom of action after the law’s commencement. All ADICO elements are present (Attribute: CSOs; Deontic: shall/shall not; Aim: accept limitations on business and political activities; Condition: ongoing after the law’s entry into force; Or-else: penalties provided elsewhere in the law). Therefore the provision is correctly coded as present (1).

Provision: PERMISSIVE GOVERNANCE PROVISION 2. [Government and agency] [must] [create or empower a dispute resolution forum] such as a court [before commencement of the law] [or else it is negligent in its duties]
Evidence: Article 9(3): "The decision on the refusal of the state registration of a charitable organization ... may be appealed against with the court."
Explanation: The cited sentence merely states that a registration refusal can be appealed to an already-existing court. Nowhere in the statute is the Government or any agency obligated to establish or formally empower a new dispute-resolution body, nor is there any requirement that this be done before the law takes effect. Because the ADICO elements of the matrix rule (government/agency duty + creation/empowerment of forum + timing) are not explicitly present, the provision is absent rather than implemented. Therefore the correct label is 0.

Provision: RESTRICTIVE GOVERNANCE PROVISION 3. [Government] [may] [create or empower cabinet minister to make new rules regulating CSOs on certain matters] [after law’s commencement] [or else leave the regulatory regime unchanged]
Evidence: Article 25: "To propose to the President of the Russian Federation and to order to the Government of the Russian Federation that they bring their legal acts into correspondence with the present Federal Law."
Explanation: Article 25 expressly instructs (and therefore authorises) the Government to issue or amend its own normative legal acts so that they comply with and implement this CSO law. This empowerment to adopt new regulatory acts will necessarily occur after the law’s commencement, fulfilling the matrix’s attribute (Government), deontic (permission/authority—indeed an obligation, which subsumes ‘may’), and aim (create new rules regulating CSOs). Hence the provision is present; the coder’s label 1 is correct, although Article 3(1) was not the best citation.

Provision: RESTRICTIVE GOVERNANCE PROVISION 6. [Non-state actors] [must not] [create new CSOs] because only the state may do so [or else face penalty for non-compliance]

Explanation: The statute imposes a binding obligation (“shall be effected”) that any body carrying out the reorganization or liquidation of a charitable organization follow the detailed procedure set out in law. The condition (when a CSO is being terminated) is present, the deontic element (“shall”) expresses a mandatory duty, and the aim is to comply with the explicit dissolution procedure. This satisfies the matrix requirement that the competent authority must follow the termination provisions, so the presence label 1 assigned by the first-round coder is correct.

Provision: RESTRICTIVE OPERATIONS PROVISION 3. [CSOs] [must not] [exceed specific threshold of budget spent on overhead] such as a certain percentage of budgets spent on administrative costs [after law’s commencement] [or else face penalty for non-compliance]

This matches every required element of the matrix provision: (1) the regulated actor (CSOs), (2) the prohibition (must not), (3) the specific overhead threshold (20 %), and (4) an implicit timing—ongoing after the law’s commencement. The optional sanction clause is not necessary. Hence the presence label (1) is correct.
